definitions.universe: instrumented bins (>=1 valid sensor reading) x days within each bin's first-to-last valid-reading span
definitions.driver_evidence: bin appears as an 'S' (stamped) stop in a trips_v6 track that day
definitions.sensor_evidence: a sensor drop event (A2) whose before-after window touches that day
definitions.neither_with_activity: no evidence from either file but >=1 valid sensor reading that day
definitions.recovered_emptying: drop event with no stamped stop for that bin on any day of its window
definitions.tonnage: drop_units/100 x bin volume (L, raw_collections; default 2500) x material mid density P32/C75/G300 kg/m3

findings: On instrumented bins the two files agree on only 14,233 bin-days (both a stamped stop and a sensor drop); the driver file alone claims 39,764 more emptying days and the sensor alone shows 32,203 more - neither record is a superset of the other.

Of the 32,203 sensor-only days, 690 (2.1%) fall on days when a v6 track did visit the bin without stamping it (logging gap); the remaining 31,513 have no recorded visit at all - off-log services or non-collection disturbances.

Of the 39,764 driver-only days, 81.9% are explained by the sensor itself - a negative-code episode (13,076) or fewer than two valid readings that day (19,477); only 7,211 days show a healthy, well-sampled sensor with no drop, the candidate false stamps.

30,504 drop events are never matched by a stamped stop on any day of their window - recovered emptyings worth an estimated 1,678.3 tonnes (drop magnitude x bin volume x material mid density), material the driver file misses entirely.

Record-level agreement between the two instruments stays flat at roughly half (39-52% by year, A2 table), so the comparison must stay at bin-day granularity; the confusion matrix, not either file alone, is the honest inventory of service events.
